###Section A: Basics of R Programming###

### Program 1: Data Exploration ###

Explanation: This program explores the built-in iris dataset. It displays the first 10 rows, last 5 rows, number of rows and columns, column names, and structure of the dataset.


```{r}
data(iris)

# Display first 10 rows
head(iris, 10)

# Display last 5 rows
tail(iris, 5)

# Number of rows and columns
nrow(iris)
ncol(iris)

# Display column names
names(iris)

# Display dataset structure
str(iris)
```
### Program 2: Variables and Data Types ###

Explanation: This program identifies the data types of the columns in mtcars. It converts the cyl and gear columns into factors and displays their frequency tables.

```{r}
data(mtcars)

# Display data types
sapply(mtcars, class)

# Convert columns into factors
mtcars$cyl <- as.factor(mtcars$cyl)
mtcars$gear <- as.factor(mtcars$gear)

# Display frequency tables
table(mtcars$cyl)
table(mtcars$gear)
```

### Program 3: Descriptive Statistics ###

Explanation: This program calculates the mean, median, minimum, maximum, and standard deviation of Sepal.Length and Petal.Length in the iris dataset.
```{r}
data(iris)

# Statistics for Sepal.Length
mean(iris$Sepal.Length)
median(iris$Sepal.Length)
min(iris$Sepal.Length)
max(iris$Sepal.Length)
sd(iris$Sepal.Length)

# Statistics for Petal.Length
mean(iris$Petal.Length)
median(iris$Petal.Length)
min(iris$Petal.Length)
max(iris$Petal.Length)
sd(iris$Petal.Length)
```

### Program 4: Missing Values ###

Explanation: This program counts missing values in each column of airquality and calculates the percentage of missing values in the Ozone and Solar.R columns.
```{r}
data(airquality)

# Count missing values in each column
colSums(is.na(airquality))

# Percentage of missing Ozone values
mean(is.na(airquality$Ozone)) * 100

# Percentage of missing Solar.R values
mean(is.na(airquality$Solar.R)) * 100
```

### Program 5: Indexing and Subsetting ###

Explanation: This program extracts the first 15 rows, selects specific columns, and displays flowers whose petal length is greater than 5.
```{r}
data(iris)

# First 15 rows
iris[1:15, ]

# Selected columns
iris[, c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", "Species")]

# Petal length greater than 5
subset(iris, Petal.Length > 5)
```

### Section B: Data Manipulation Using dplyr ###

### Program 6: Filter Rows ###
Explanation: This program filters cars with mileage greater than 20 and horsepower below 100. It displays only the required four columns.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
data(mtcars)

mtcars %>%
  filter(mpg > 20, hp < 100) %>%
  select(mpg, hp, wt, cyl)
```

###Program 7: Select and Arrange ###

Explanation: This program selects the species, sepal length, and petal length columns from iris. It arranges the results in descending order of petal length.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
data(iris)

iris %>%
  select(Species, Sepal.Length, Petal.Length) %>%
  arrange(desc(Petal.Length))
```

### Program 8: Create New Variables ###

Explanation: This program creates a new variable called power_to_weight by dividing horsepower by weight. It displays the five cars with the highest ratios.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
data(mtcars)

mtcars %>%
  mutate(power_to_weight = hp / wt) %>%
  arrange(desc(power_to_weight)) %>%
  head(5)
```

### Program 9: Group By and Summarise ###

Explanation: This program groups flowers by species and calculates the mean and standard deviation of sepal length and petal length for each species.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
data(iris)

iris %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Sepal = mean(Sepal.Length),
    SD_Sepal = sd(Sepal.Length),
    Mean_Petal = mean(Petal.Length),
    SD_Petal = sd(Petal.Length)
  )
```

### Program 10: Multiple Operations ###

Explanation: This program groups cars by the number of cylinders and calculates the number of cars, average mileage, average horsepower, and maximum weight. The results are arranged by average mileage in descending order.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
data(mtcars)

mtcars %>%
  group_by(cyl) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Cars = n(),
    Average_MPG = mean(mpg),
    Average_HP = mean(hp),
    Maximum_Weight = max(wt)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Average_MPG))
```

### Section C: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) ###

### Program 11: Summary Analysis ###

Explanation: This program generates a statistical summary of the iris dataset and identifies the numerical variable with the highest standard deviation.
```{r}
data(iris)

# Statistical summary
summary(iris)

# Standard deviations of numerical columns
sds <- sapply(iris[, 1:4], sd)
print(sds)

# Variable with the highest standard deviation
names(sds)[which.max(sds)]
```

### Program 12: Correlation Analysis ###

Explanation: This program calculates the correlations between mileage, horsepower, weight, and displacement. It identifies the pair with the strongest absolute correlation, excluding each variable's correlation with itself.
```{r}
data(mtcars)

x <- mtcars[, c("mpg", "hp", "wt", "disp")]

# Correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(x)
print(cor_matrix)

# Find the strongest absolute correlation
cor_matrix[lower.tri(cor_matrix, diag = TRUE)] <- NA

index <- which(
  abs(cor_matrix) == max(abs(cor_matrix), na.rm = TRUE),
  arr.ind = TRUE
)

rownames(cor_matrix)[index[1, 1]]
colnames(cor_matrix)[index[1, 2]]
```

### Program 13: Data Visualization ###

Explanation: This program creates three graphs using iris: a histogram of sepal length, a boxplot of petal length by species, and a scatter plot showing the relationship between sepal length and petal length.
```{r}
data(iris)

# Histogram
hist(iris$Sepal.Length,
     main = "Sepal Length",
     xlab = "Sepal Length",
     col = "lightblue")

# Boxplot
boxplot(Petal.Length ~ Species,
        data = iris,
        main = "Petal Length by Species",
        xlab = "Species",
        ylab = "Petal Length",
        col = c("pink", "lightgreen", "lightblue"))

# Scatter plot
plot(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Petal.Length,
     col = as.numeric(iris$Species),
     pch = 19,
     xlab = "Sepal Length",
     ylab = "Petal Length",
     main = "Sepal Length vs Petal Length")

legend("topleft",
       legend = levels(iris$Species),
       col = 1:3,
       pch = 19)
```

### Program 14: Outlier Detection Using IQR ###

Explanation: This program detects outliers in the Ozone column of airquality using the Interquartile Range (IQR) method. Missing values are removed before calculating the bounds.
```{r}
data(airquality)

x <- na.omit(airquality$Ozone)

Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25)
Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75)
IQR_value <- IQR(x)

lower <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_value
upper <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_value

outliers <- x[x < lower | x > upper]

cat("Lower Bound:", lower, "\n")
cat("Upper Bound:", upper, "\n")
cat("Number of Outliers:", length(outliers), "\n")

print(outliers)
```

### Program 15: Group Comparison Using ToothGrowth ###

Explanation: This program calculates the mean and median tooth length for each combination of supplement type and dose. It also creates a boxplot to compare tooth growth among the groups.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
data(ToothGrowth)

# Calculate mean and median
ToothGrowth %>%
  group_by(supp, dose) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Length = mean(len),
    Median_Length = median(len),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Create boxplot
boxplot(len ~ interaction(supp, dose),
        data = ToothGrowth,
        main = "Tooth Growth Comparison",
        xlab = "Supplement and Dose",
        ylab = "Tooth Length",
        col = "lightblue")
```

### Section D: Control Statements in R ###


### Program 16: if-else Statement ###

Explanation: This program classifies cars into high, moderate, or low mileage categories according to their mpg values. It displays each car's name and category.
```{r}
data(mtcars)

for (i in 1:nrow(mtcars)) {
  mpg <- mtcars$mpg[i]

  if (mpg >= 25) {
    category <- "High mileage"
  } else if (mpg >= 15) {
    category <- "Moderate mileage"
  } else {
    category <- "Low mileage"
  }

  cat(rownames(mtcars)[i], "-", category, "\n")
}
```

### Program 17: for Loop ###

Explanation: This program uses a for loop to calculate the average sepal length separately for each species in the iris dataset.
```{r}
data(iris)

for (sp in levels(iris$Species)) {
  avg <- mean(
    iris$Sepal.Length[iris$Species == sp]
  )

  cat("Species:", sp,
      "Average Sepal Length:", avg, "\n")
}
```

### Program 18: while Loop ###

Explanation: This program examines the first 10 cars in mtcars using a while loop. Each car is classified as fuel-efficient if its mileage is greater than 20; otherwise, it is classified as less fuel-efficient.
```{r}
data(mtcars)

i <- 1

while (i <= 10) {
  car <- rownames(mtcars)[i]
  mpg <- mtcars$mpg[i]

  if (mpg > 20) {
    category <- "Fuel-efficient"
  } else {
    category <- "Less fuel-efficient"
  }

  cat(car, "-", category, "\n")

  i <- i + 1
}
```

### Program 19: Conditional Filtering ###

Explanation: This program uses if-else statements to classify non-missing ozone observations as low, moderate, or high. It then counts the observations in each category.
```{r}
data(airquality)

low <- 0
moderate <- 0
high <- 0

for (i in 1:nrow(airquality)) {
  ozone <- airquality$Ozone[i]

  if (!is.na(ozone)) {
    if (ozone < 30) {
      low <- low + 1
    } else if (ozone <= 60) {
      moderate <- moderate + 1
    } else {
      high <- high + 1
    }
  }
}

cat("Low:", low, "\n")
cat("Moderate:", moderate, "\n")
cat("High:", high, "\n")
```

### Program 20: Integrated Programming Challenge ###

Explanation: This program filters flowers with petal length greater than 4, groups them by species, and calculates the number of flowers and average petal length. It then classifies each species based on whether its average petal length exceeds 4.5 and arranges the results in descending order.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
data(iris)

result <- iris %>%
  filter(Petal.Length > 4) %>%
  group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Flowers = n(),
    Average_Petal_Length = mean(Petal.Length),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Category = ifelse(
      Average_Petal_Length > 4.5,
      "High Average Petal Length",
      "Low Average Petal Length"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Average_Petal_Length))

print(result)
```
